title: H-alpha fits do not show the 63 km/s CCF shift in four GJ 357 HARPS exposures
abstract: Four GJ 357 exposures have cross-correlation velocities near -97 km/s in HARPS RVBank version 02. We test a common stellar velocity shift with a separate H-alpha estimator and new fits to the four public spectra. All 53 catalog exposures have unique ESO matches with CCF values equal to rounding precision. After a normal line offset is removed, the four H-alpha and CCF values differ by 62.57 to 63.51 km/s. Three control cuts give the same result within 0.02 km/s. Sixteen new line fits give -35.77 to -35.06 km/s. Gaussian and Lorentzian profiles in two regions reduce squared residuals by 51 to 62 percent against fits restricted near the CCF velocity. This opposes a common Doppler shift of the dominant spectrum and supports a false CCF solution. The exact fault is open. Shared HARPS spectra, possible blends and line effects limit inference. No independent telescope or planet test is supplied. Code, aggregate evidence, exact hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: H-alpha lacks the extreme CCF shift. The left panel retains failed finite control fits. The right panel shows full velocity ranges over four suspect exposures; these are not error bars.
